feed.title: James Wiesebron
feed.subtitle: Essays on runtime alignment: keeping AI agents doing what you intended while they run.

entry.title: "Nothing to decide" is a claim
entry.summary: Agents settle questions that were yours when asking costs more than deciding. Track every decision until a person answers it, and make an agent that reports none list what it considered.

entry.title: Attention is all you need (to protect)
entry.summary: Human attention is the scarcest resource in AI-assisted work. AI output can spend it or save it, and people can only choose where to spend it once they trust what the agent did.

entry.title: Runtime alignment
entry.summary: Runtime alignment means keeping an agent doing what you intended while it runs. Intentional agentic work is how to get there: answer each predictable failure with structure.

entry.title: Give agents a contract, not a conversation
entry.summary: When intent lives in a chat, agents drift. A contract that each role can only partly edit keeps agent work aligned and makes "done" mean something.

entry.title: Reseed, don't compact
entry.summary: Long agent work shouldn't depend on a summarizer deciding what to forget. Keep a small, fixed core that holds the intent, and rebuild from it on purpose.

entry.title: Agreement isn't verification
entry.summary: When AI reviewers agree, that tells you their reasoning hangs together, not that the work is right. How to build review that checks the work.

entry.title: Teams, not swarms
entry.summary: A group of agents in a shared chat is a swarm. A team needs a protocol: who reviews whom, how approvals stay current, and checks that turn known deadlocks into rules.

entry.title: The model owns judgment, code owns the clock
entry.summary: Models are good at judgment and unreliable at bookkeeping. Let plain code run the loop, and call the model only when there's something to decide.

entry.title: Stop telling AI agents what not to do
entry.summary: A prompt that says "don't" is a suggestion. The safer move is to take the capability away, and let the wall explain itself.

entry.title: Connectors with enforceable boundaries
entry.summary: Agents get useful when they connect to your tickets, wikis, documents and email. How to design those connections so they can't be misused, even by a confused or manipulated agent.
